lines.text: Subtitle created by - Aorion - "The Odyssey (1997)" Synced by LoopFroots.
We need to get her to the palace.
Odysseus. Master, the baby is coming!
Just think of us. just you and I.
Hold tight. Give me the pain.
It is coming. It is coming. Odysseus.
You must get her to the palace. It is coming.
Oh, the queen. Queen Penelope's baby...
Hold me. Hold me. Hold me in your eyes.
This day was the proudest day of my life.
My sweet Penelope and the gods had given me a son.
But at the same moment, the world we built together was changed forever.
Dark news was coming to my shores.
My beloved Greece was at war with Troy.
A kingdom, far across the seas.
The mightiest of my fellow kings, Agamemnon and Menelaus themselves, came for me.
Sworn to a blood oath of allegiance. and bound by honor to protect my land, I was forced to leave my home, not knowing if I would ever see my wife and child again.
I am Odysseus, king of Ithica.
The bow. Now, belongs to your son.
You alone, will teach him to string it when he is grown.
Summon the captains. Assemble the crews.
Athena, my goddess, you have always protected me.
Tell me. Is there no way to avoid this war?
Promise me you will return. I cannot.
Troy does not fall so gently.
Penelope, If I cannot return ... You will!
If I fail and if I die.
Don't even say the words, don't.
You must allow me to die inside of your.
You cannot live a life alone.
If there is a beard on his face and I still hadn't come,
And you will give our son a kingdom.
And all we have worked for.
Alive like this tree around which we built this world.
Return with the spoils of enemies you slain.
Give Penelope the same strength you gave to me.
I will care for your son as I cared for you.
The gods of sea and sky carried me towards Troy.
You're really, Eurylochus! He is infected with a lying sickness.
I am telling you, it's true.
The walls of Troy reach to the clouds.
I see you are no longer with me, Athena.
Ha. Is that any way to speak to your protector?
I think the wine swells your head, my Odysseus.
Are you drinking because you fear your future?
Me? I am afraid of nothing.
I am teasing you. You are anger with me.
Athena. You could have only persuaded Agamemnon, on the day of my son's birth, no less.
I am a goddess after all. I have other duties.
And don't forget. I can be seen by whom I choose.
I did not want you to escape this journey, because I want you to go.
I want you, my brave Odysseus, to defeat the Trojans.
No, your destiny is to do battle to become immortal.
To have your name on the lips of endless generations.
No. I have no need to be remembered by endless generations.
Odysseus. You cannot lie to me. I know your true character.
You even surround yourself with men who would not refuse you.
Look at them. I fear for you.
Giant Polites, he is stubborn beyond words.
Eurylochus, lies even more than you.
Eurylochus is the best blacksmith in all Greece.
Anticlus. His curiosity will always bring him trouble.
You see the good in them because they love you.
You must use this scope to defeat the Trojans.
You must be brave, my Odysseus.
I have no fear as long as you are with me.
Year after year, we fought beneath Troy's walls.
I stood with the mighty Achilles, fight to fight against Hector.
The Trojan's most ferocious warrior, and his troops.
Thousands of men died where they fell.
While mothers and wives spent endless sleepless nights.
And no one knew whose side the gods were on.
It is I, Hector, defender of Troy, who challenge you.
Here, before the gods and your own people, I will tear open your chest suck out your beating heart... and spit your blood in the faces of your slaves.
Achilles, god among man, was slain.
Troy, had taken the best of us and still remain locked.
The word on each Greek soldiers' lips was : Surrender.
But I refused to accept so much death in vain.
There was a way to enter Troy.
Let me go! Let me go!
Mercy, good king. Have mercy on an old man.
It was I who convinced the Greeks to retreat.
I told them to make this offering to you, great king.
To my brothers, after 10 years of war, you have won. and no one will ever enter the walls of Troy.
I convinced them to build this mighty horse, as a gift of surrender to you.
And for my troubles, they branded me a coward.
And left me here to beg. Good.
Mighty Priam, give me life. And I'll be your slave.
Any fool can see that he is lying!
That man has never spoken the truth!
Beware the Greeks, and their gifts!
Beware! Poseidon has sent his sea serpent.
Your soothsayer has offended Poseidon with his lies!
You must accept the Greeks' gift!
Do you see? You gods of sea and sky.
A mortal man of flesh and blood and bone and mind!
I do not need you now.
Odysseus, why do you defy me?
It is I, Poseidon. God of the wine dark sea.
You have already forgotten how I helped you.
For 10 years, you played with us as with toys.
For 10 years, you let blood spilled your shores!
But it was my serpent who silenced Laocoon or your horse was doomed.
Yet, you refuse to give thanks.
You forget a man is nothing without the gods.
You will suffer for this offense.
For your arrogance, you will drift on my sea for an eternity.
Never again will you reach the shores of Ithaca.
No one will stop me from seeing Ithaca.
Victorious, defiant, I sailed from Troy.
My mind filled only with the thoughts of the home.
I had not seen for 10 years.
You see, Telemachus. It is easy.
Telemachus, where are you? You can't catch me.
And yes, I will. Ha ha ha.
You won't catch me. You won't catch me.
Where are you suppose to be?
He is not ready for man's work.
Because you would not let him grow.
He is my son, not yours! My son was ready for all things.
Yes, your son had his father.
It can never be soon enough.
Each day without Odysseus last forever.
But ... if he does not return.
Do not say those words to me.
If Odysseus is dead you must bear it and go on.
You must live for your son.
You have a heart of stone.
Yes, if stone can shiver and bleed.
Poseidon began his revenge soon enough.
For months, he blanketed the sea in fog.
Separated from the rest of the fleet, I was lost.
When I find you, you and your flute are in the sea.
If men live here, they can tell us how far we wondered.
Let the others go, master. You can follow if they meet anyone.
And I bet I am the first to find them.
Bring me gifts, for our host.
You stay with the ship. And let you go alone, master?
No women, but... plenty of cheese.
They keep sheep in this cave with them.
We will trade it for water.
Mixed wine with water, you pig. It's too strong without.
No. We will roll you down the hill when you are drunk.
We bring gifts, that is the custom in this part of the world, no?
That is- That is the law.
Here, we have no law. Here, we do what we want!
No, my brothers' at the big caves.
Our mother is a sea nymph.
Our father is the mighty god, Poseidon.
I am the youngest, Polyphemes. What did you bring?
If you would share some sheep, we could cook you a feast.
Because, man do not eat one another.
Of course, if you do, then... you would eat all the magic inside my head .
Do you know how much magic I have in here?
I will spit your head out!
But you would have learned nothing.
You eat me, then you kill all the secrets of the world.
What is it? Aye. It's wine.
It's a drink of the gods.
What is your name? My name?
He is the lord of... Please!
In the morning, you will tell me more secrets, after I eat.
And after he's dead, who would move the stone?
There must be another way out.
What have you done to me?
Help! Help me, I cannot see!
Where are you? Where are you?
I'll kill you all and eat you piece by piece!
I will get you! Where are you?
You can't escape! I will get you!
Blame your father, Poseidon! It is he who made me blind you!
You hear, Poseidon! I am alive!
Odysseus is alive and you cannot stop me!
We sailed for months, from cyclops island to the setting sun.
Our hearts heavy with the lost of Antiphus and his gentle flute.
Our mouths dry with thirst, desperate for water to drink, we approached another unknown land.
I can see you are surprised.
I am Aeolus, god of wind.
This is my island, where soft breezes and raging tempest... all begin.
Well, I am honored. But... why do you not allow me to drink?
Because I know you, Odysseus, lord of Ithaca.
Do not be afraid. Step through the water.
The great hero who built the Trojan horse.
But... few Greeks know that you are the only one who can't go home.
Poseidon still believes he can stop me.
Poseidon. Poseidon. Poseidon this, Poseidon that.
Poseidon is a bully He's my cousin. He's arrogant, he's selfish.
He forgets that the sea is nothing with the wind.
And who is the god of the wind?
Guess who is the god of the winds?
We'll get back at him. Give me this.
I  have left only the West wind free.
In 9 days, it will blow you and your ship to Ithaca.
Because you are the first mortal ever to use his mind!
And you understand that there is always something to learn!
And you better not open that sack.
We find water. He finds gold.
I will tell you when we reach Ithaca, not before.
Soon. Aeolus had promised me Soon, I will see my Penelope, my family, my home.
Tell Penelope I would not sleep till we embrace in my bed.
I am afraid to say it.
It must be full of treasure.
What do you say it is? I don't care.
You cannot open it. It is the master's.
What is the master's is ours. Odysseus can keep it.
I just wanted to see it. Well, I'll have a share of it too.
I must wake the master. No.
Move, and I will cut your head off.
Once we land he will never show us what's in that sack.
I told you. I told you not to open this till Ithaca!
Are you fools? You betrayed me!
I have held Ithaca in my eyes.
Only to have my hopes of reaching Penelope crushed by the fury of the unlocked winds.
Tossed in the storm, all food and water lost.
We were set down now, on the far side of the world.
Here, master, all I could find.
You will not get 1 kernel from me.
You act alone and you starve alone.
If there is game here I will kill it. But I...
I will share it with my brothers.
It's you who open the sack and now we all starve.
I can cut you open too.
We will cook you right here. Hm.
Aim for it! And come on, stop it!
Get in front! Get the pig!
Eurylochus, enough of your games. It is the truth! I swear it!
This is the island of a witch, a sorceress!
She turned all our brothers into animals.
I saw it with my own eyes! He is lying to protect himself!
What did you do, coward? Run from the fight?
For half a day we climbed up a path into these mountains.
From the woods, suddenly we heard a sweet woman's voice.
Singing, calling us in. The witch.
We came to a stone palace, surrounded by animals: lions, wolves.
We saw her from a distance , walking from window to window, singing her song.
She offered food and wine in her honeyed voice,
and in they went. But you did not go.
And never have I felt worst for being right!
I crept closer and saw there was music. The witch waved her hands and each one of our brothers was turned into an animal before my eyes!
It does look like Polites. Quiet, fool!
Are we to starve because of his lies.
I will kill your with my bare hands! Move. Get off!
All this is true? On my life.
If I do not return by sunrise, leave this place.
She will cast a spell over you!
Stay away! Don't come any closer!
You're about to lose your sword, and you need it.
Sorry. I'm not allow to touch.
Heed my advice, and reach that stone.
I'm giving it to you. A god to a mortal No, I refuse.
But it is the only way to stop the witch, Circe's spell.
But now, When you drink her honey potion, you will remain a man.
This will catch the witch off guard.
Draw you sword, as if to kill her.
Frighten her a little! Then she will make you an offer, to take her to bed.
Only then, will she surrender your men.
Come on! Come, you're almost there.
Come on. Come on. Come on. Don't be afraid.
You must be hungry and thirsty.
I've hope for a lion for such a man.
Well. You will not change me.
What would you do with this knife?
Do... and you will never see your men again.
The only way I will turn your soldiers back to man is if you take me to bed.
I am telling you, you are gutless murderers.
At least our bellies will be full!
I believe you, Eurylochus, but I cannot stop them all!
I'm going to have your share.
Polites! I told you it was Polites!
You will regret for this! Polites!
You will remember me! And he will remember you!
Circe, filled our ears with music and our minds with magical lotus blossom.
Her potions are weakening our bodies and clouding our thoughts.
I'm going hunting. Not with that!
If I am old enough to keep my father's flocks and kill his game,
then I am old enough to use his bow. If you can string it. it's your's to hunt with.
If you cannot, you will place it in your father's treasury until I give it to you.
Mistress  Anticlea is going to the shore! Come quickly!
Anticlea! I can wait no longer.
I will meet him in the sea. He is alive.
We will wait for him together. Together.
But my stone heart has broken.
I have nothing left to bleed!
What of your family? Of me?
You are not only the mother of my husband, You are my mother. You are my father.
You will feel me with you.
Even... from the land of the dead.
You lie with me yet you think of your wife.
While we shared this bed, you've forgotten her.
You have given me much, Circe.
But no bare enough flesh could ever make me forget Penelope.
He thinks he has been here 5 days when it has been 5 years.
You mortals understand so little here, in my palace.
It passes, slips by, fades, however I choose.
What seem like a day to you, even an hour was a year outside these walls.
I saw the sun rise and set, that's impossible.
If you needed proof to you eyes, go see your ship buried in 5 years of tide.
And on the way, wonder if your wife's memory is as strong as yours!
Or if she has found another partner!
You conspired with Poseidon against me!
Don't blame the gods for your deeds.
You were given your men back, and yet, you lingered in my bed.
15 years, I have not seen my son and my home.
You lose much more than 5 years if you don’t open your eyes and see what you are.
No! You, open your eyes and you see who I am!
Now, you help me fine my way home or curse them I'll kill you.
I know one man who knows the way to Ithaca.
Tiresias, the prophet. Tiresias is dead.
If you still wish to go home, you must first, enter the underworld.
Only there, will you find the answers you seek.
You are right to be afraid.
You must cross the river of fire and sacrifice a ram,
and you must enter the fire
You have brought news of my father?
You cannot say that, there is no proof!
Everyone who fought at Troy has long returned home.
Either Lord Odysseus is dead, lost in Poseidon's graveyard, or he has chose not to return, to abandon your mother, his kingdom, and you.
Now, your mother will choose one of us and marry again.
They say they're here for you.
Men who say my father is dead!
They have brought gifts, I must receive them. And you must.
I will respect this as you father did, and so will you!
The nobles of Ithaca will beg at your feet.
I will receive these men, and that is all.
They will have nothing which belongs to Odysseus.
Not his fortunes and not his wife.
I know you would follow me now.
The time has not come to enter this house.
We've suffered the lost of many men, together.
And now, we may never be in each other's eyes ever again.
You will be back. And if I'm not?
We will not reach Ithaca without you!
And if I do not return, you row, row without end.
This ram is not for you!
You have risked much to seek a blind prophet.
Bring the ram forward, offer it up.
You are a clever man, Odysseus of Ithaca, but not a very wise one.
You keep your eyes only on your home.
Blinded, you do not see that it is the journey itself which makes up your life.
Only when you understand this will you understand the meaning of wisdom.
The answer has been before your eyes, every night at sea.
On this side of Poseidon's realm, there is a constellation which never sinks beneath the horizon, shapes like a hunter.
And there, You will reach the Strait of Scylla and Charybdis.
On one side, there is a creature, vile, ferocious.
Insatiable for blood, she lurks in the shadows hoping to fill her belly.
She invites you in, but she is a thing of terror, Odysseus.
When she opens her gaping mouth, you and all with you, will be swallowed by her force! Ha-ha-ha.
I took my own life out of grief.
I could wait no longer for you.
She is waiting for you. Where?
Men are trying to steal your world.
Penelope was alive and waiting for me.
But my mother's words burned my soul.
Men would stop at nothing to steal my kingdom.
Who's this thing? Look at this fool!
You are Queen Penelope? I am the wife of king Odysseus.
I have come I am here
I bring gifts of gold and wool, and music, and jugglers to your palace.
I hope my father died a hero.
If he is alive, he has forgotten me.
The day the gods gave you to us, they took your father from me.
But he promised me, with you lying here in my arms, that he would return alive, as this tree around which we built own world is alive.
If he's alive, why hasn't he come?
I know your father. He is alive.
There is something you must know.
The day you father sailed, I swore to him a promise that if he had not returned by the time you were a man, beard on your chin, that I must remarry.
You do not have your beard yet.
Take me to your mistress, I need to talk to her.
All here, believe Odysseus, king of Ithaca is died.
Today, I will begin to weave a shroud for my lost husband.
If he is not seen in Ithaca before I finished I will choose one of you to take his place beside me.
I will send for maidens to help you.
I alone, must do this work.
We will be old man by the time you finish.
You have brought gifts to my door.
I have given you a proper feast in return.
Now I depend on your Honor. Return to your homes.
When my work is done, you will hear my decision.
We will stay where we are.
We will not leave here until you choose.
Your husband's wine is very good.
Winter turn to summer as we neared the Straits of Scylla and Charybdis.
After a 16 year ordeal, nothing could frighten me or my warriors.
But we have never seen what waited between those rocks.
Give me a torch! Give me a torch!
This tapestry will never be finish.
I will take the work if you wish. No!
I will serve these filthy strangers no longer.
I have to crawl over that pig, Elatus, each time I went open the treasury!
And to watch men from our own island eat you and Telemachus out of house and home!
It's more than I can bear.
At least there is life here now. Melanthe, quiet.
I have seen the way you went after that snake, Eurymachus He asked me to serve him.
I cannot refuse my mistress's guest. Guest?
We much longer can we stand this?
How much longer do we have to take, you pigs! Calm down, Eurycleia. Calm down.
Stop it. Listen to me. You pigs!
Listen, I've ordered you! Do not tempt me!
You can't drive them away. They are man.
They will follow their empty bellies.
My men lost before my eyes.
I float endlessly on Poseidon sea.
Wondering when he will take my life.
I need water. Bring him water.
No one comes or goes from my island.
I must-I must find a way home.
Please do not mind my maids.
You are the first man they have seen in their lives.
I myself, have not laid eyes on one for over 100 years.
What are you doing here in the dark?
I got to kill Antinous. All of them if I have to.
Antinous is a warrior, he's been to battle.
He has cut man in two with his sword!
You have not done that yet. Now is the time.
If you kill him, the others will not leave.
You will give them an excuse to turn against you.
Then tell me, what can I do?
Do as your father would do.
Call on those who are still loyal to him for help.
Call the assembly? Who am I?
In the name of Athena... In the name of Athena...
I am Mentor, keeper of the staff.
I have long, long, long awaited for this day.
It is I, Prince Telemachus, son of Odysseus, King of Ithaca, who summoned you to this place.
An army of suitors has invaded my palace.
They slaughtered my oxen, my pigs, my sheep to feast on.
Soon, I will have nothing to eat myself.
They offer no proof of my father's death, yet seek to take his place.
And before my mother's eyes, they beat my servants and rape my maids!
I ask you. Men of Ithaca.
Help me rid my house of these shameless thieves!
We suitors, have broken no law, taken nothing which was not rightfully ours!
We brought our precious gifts, and she took them with open arms!
Now she must choose between us which is right.
Not one of us should spill blood over pigs and sheep.
We can do no more. Let us go.
Kill me. I can see it.
If you will not help me, then give me a ship.
I will sail from Ithaca and find my father.
The boy should not be punished.
If he wishes a ship, we will give him a ship.
You will have your ship, Telemachus. You will have your ship, Telemachus!
You have a reason for this? He will end like his father.
And if he returns? We will greet him, with the spear in his back.
When I touch you skin, I wonder how you got this scar.
The day Achilles was taken from us.
From a battle. A wild boar.
I was 15... and my mother cried tears of happiness.
You were going to leave without even thanking me for my kindness.
Don't you see. No one leaves my island!
And all that live here exist to serve me.
Perhaps, in another 10 years, perhaps never.
You did not say goodbye to your mother.
The sorrow is on your face.
You are right to fear the sea. I am not afraid!
I have never set foot from Ithaca.
Do not worry. The gods are watching you.
They gods have cursed me. Oh, oh, oh.
Since the day I was born. Ha-ha-ha.
Your head is as hard as your father's.
When I wish to be, yes.
You spoke very well at your assembly.
You kept your wits and used them wisely to get the ship.
But you did not help me.
Remember. The gods will not do for man, what man must do for himself.
Go, before the ship sails without you.
I have never cross the sea. Where should I go?
What would I say to such a man?
Use your wits. I will guide you.
For 2 more years, Calypso's island was my prison.
Forgotten by the outside world, abandon by Athena.
My hopes of ever reaching Penelope began to fade.
Oh. Calypso, the concealer is not overjoy to see me?
Calypso. I am only a messenger.
Who loves to bring painful news.
I have given him a home!
It is not Odysseus' fate to end his days on your island.
You are to set him free without delay.
These are the words from the lips of Zeus himself.
Neither Zeus nor any god pity Odysseus, it is envy which sends you here.
They are all outraged by me openly making love to a mortal man.
Choosing him as my husband. Calypso.
It is I, who pulled him from the sea, who tended to his wounds.
You're all are jealous of my happiness!
Offer this man his freedom or your island will be driven to the bottom of Poseidon sea.
They will not try to stop you.
A moment ago, you left this cave with so much love in your eyes.
Now, you want me to leave?
You are no longer worthy of me.
You must help me build a ship.
On the far side of the island, in a cave there is dry wood.
Washed onto the shore as you were, as you were.
You are not afraid of me.
I only wanted to offer you some wine.
What keeps your mistress from finishing her tapestry?
Come on, where is that girl?
Where's the boy? Send the boy.
I do not mean to frighten you tend to your room but I had to see.
Now, your deceit can only bring trouble.
I will not speak a word, but your maid, she may tell another.
You will not trick them much longer.
It has been too long since you felt a man's touch.
Take my. End this siege tonight.
These other men, they come for your fortune.
I will wait for his return, or till my son brings proof.
It is I, who have no choice.
You may stay if you choose to.
You wife has aged during these years, Odysseus.
She will not match my beauty.
No mortal woman could ever match you.
And she has aged as I have.
And when I reach Ithaca we will grow old together.
With me, you will never grow old.
I would rather lie in my wife's arms for one moment as a man, than to live forever without her.
Who is this boy, my son brings?
There is the king. Now, go.
I've traveled long and far to meet you.
Oh. You have your father's searching eyes The same thoughtful forehead.
You are Odysseus' son, you are his son.
I sailed from Ithaca to find him.
I saw you on the day you were born.
It was the proudest and most painful day of your father's life.
We fought at Troy, side by side.
He freed us to return to Greece.
But... he will never see his home again.
Not one day, not one hour pass for Odysseus of Troy, with you and your mother in his heart.
Only death could stop him returning to Ithaca.
You must fight for what is his. and yours.
What do you want from me?
I want you to suffer much more.
All that is left is my life!
My goal is not to kill you.
What do you want from me?
What do you want me to understand?
That without gods, man is nothing.
Broken by Poseidon's waves and still far from Ithaca, but I was alive.
I have reached Phaeacia, the land of mariners and fishermen.
Unsure whether I will be welcomed, I was lead to the palace of their ruler, the powerful king...
I shared with you my food.
Now, will you share with me
My name has long been cursed.
To let it leave my lips would only cause you pain.
I know only one long lost hero, who being curse by the gods could survive.
I never dreamed I would see Odysseus himself.
It's an honor to all Phaeacie that such a hero as Odysseus of Ithaca, sits among us.
I will give my finest ship heavy with gifts and food, and the finest mariners of all Phaeacie, to sail you safely home.
The Phaeacians carried me towards Ithaca.
But it was Poseidon, who allowed me to continue my journey to consider his words.
I understood that I was only 1 man in the world.
His body will fail him in Ithaca.
He left a year ago to look for you. Go. Go, bring him here.
Tell me.  How's my mother? She will be overjoy to see you.
But come, tell me of your journey.
Later, I must go to her.
Who is it? Who is there?
Do not dare say those words! Come out of there!
Odysseus is dead! Odysseus is alive and he's standing before you.
I see only a man, with no respect for a son's feelings.
No, no. You are my son, and these are the hands, here, which brought you into this world, here.
for all the world to see.
I showed you your home for the first time.
And then I was taken from you and your mother.
I placed you in her arms in our bed which I give her to with these hands.
She must have told you this.
These men have got black hearts! They fear nothing!
They will all run like dogs now. Yes!
Eumaeus, bring them food for the feast.
I'll never feed them again. Never!
You... will do as you have always done.
They were given to me out of the suitors men.
Tell them you will join them later.
But tell no one I have come.
That's why I love you, my Odysseus.
Any other man, after so many years, would have rushed home to embrace his wife and children.
